newsitem.title: GERMANY: German SPD slams plan for labour office savings.
newsitem.headline: German SPD slams plan for labour office savings.

text.p: Germany's opposition Social Democrats (SPD) on Sunday criticised government plans to cut the budget deficit by slashing funding for training and job creation, as reported by a news magazine at the weekend.
According to Der Spiegel magazine, Finance Minister Theo Waigel wants to reduce funding to the Federal Labour Office by over two billion marks ($1.2 billion) during the second half of this year.

SPD parliamentary leader Rudolf Scharping told German radio such cuts would lead to a surge in unemployment by a further 200,000. Scharping said Waigel should make cuts elsewhere by trimming bureaucracy and subsidies as well as tax breaks.
The report of Waigel's plans came a day after the labour office reported German unemployment rose 56,000 to a seasonally adjusted 4,358,000 in May.

Scharping said the SPD was against raising petrol or value added taxes to solve Waigel's budget problems, which the finance minister is struggling to resolve to qualify Germany for Europe's single currency.

Scharping said the entry criteria and timetable for the euro must be kept to, but said economically it did not matter whether Germany had a budget deficit to gross domestic product ratio of 2.9 percent or 3.1 percent. ($ = 1.725 German Marks)
